item.description:
What's new in 3.2.0

A pane's file browser answers a right-click now, with the things a file list is expected to do — Finder, the clipboard, the paths, the Trash. Load Context works on a server: the clock button lists the conversations that folder has had on the far machine, not just on this Mac. And a pane no longer goes quiet while its agent still has subagents working.

Right-click in a pane's files — ⌘E

  • A row's menu says the keyboard's verbs in words — Open, Quick Look, Reveal in Files — and adds what no key here does: Show in Finder, Copy, the paths, and Move to Trash.
  • Copy puts the file itself on the pasteboard, so ⌘V in Finder is a copy of it rather than its name as text.
  • Copy Relative Path is the one to know about beside a running agent — the agent is already standing in the root everything here is relative to, so Dax/Tools/… is what belongs in the prompt rather than /Users/….
  • Move to Trash, with no confirmation sheet. It goes to the Trash, which is undone from the Finder you already have open — the same bargain Finder makes with the same key.
  • A server's menu is shorter, and honestly so. Finder, the pasteboard's file flavour and the Trash are all this Mac talking about a file that is on this Mac; a remote row gets Download…, Quick Look — which fetches a copy first, exactly as the space bar does — and the paths. There is no rm down an ssh hiding behind an item that reads as recoverable.
  • Right-clicking the space between the rows asks about the folder instead: Go Up, Show as Grid or List, Show Hidden Files, Refresh, Show in Finder, and the folder's path. The header's eye and grid toggles are findable once you know what they are; this is where you look when you don't.

Load Context, on a server

  • The clock button now appears on a pane whose herd is on a server and lists every conversation that folder has had over there — grouped by when, one click to type the chosen one into the prompt.
  • The traces are on the far disk, where the scan that reads ~/.claude/projects on this Mac finds nothing and would say the folder has no history. They come back in one connection instead, heads and tails, and are read here.
  • Same gesture as it has always been on this Mac: load, not copy — the clipboard never sees it, and Return is left for you to press.

A pane that is still working says so

  • An agent running subagents no longer reads as idle. The hold already watched for the "N shell(s) still running" line Claude Code leaves under its prompt; the same footer says "N local agents still running" when the work in flight is subagents, and that case is covered now too.
  • It survives a narrow pane. The screen is read as it is drawn, so a wrap put a line break where the space was and the check missed it — a tile in a herd of four is routinely that narrow.

Around the app

  • Signed, notarized, universal (Apple Silicon & Intel), macOS 14+.
